name: PCL-EC
bestUses: Printed electrical conductors, contacts, heaters, antennas and EMI shielding are the maker's proposed applications (Multi3D Electrifi).
limitations: Its polymer is inferred, so it names no estimate identity and is not estimated. Its maker keeps it to about 45 °C in service and advises a direct-drive extruder with a short filament path, not a multi-material feed system.
identityNote: Inferred filing. Multi3D's Electrifi is a "copper-filled thermoplastic"; its safety data sheet lists "biodegradable polyester" and "Conductive Filler" and gives a melting point of "Approximately 60 °C". Polycaprolactone (PCL, melting point 60 °C in polymers.csv) is the one biodegradable polyester that melts near 60 °C (polybutylene succinate and adipate-terephthalate melt near 115 °C, PLA from 150 °C), and the maker's 140-160 °C nozzle, room-temperature bed and "soft, low-modulus filament" are a PCL's. The maker names no polymer, so the filing is the best evidence; a maker document naming another polyester moves the product.

products.composition: "Highly conductive copper-filled thermoplastic filament" with "a percolated copper network embedded in a thermoplastic matrix" (R-MULTI3D-ELECTRIFI-TDS, p. 1); its safety data sheet lists "biodegradable polyester" and "Conductive Filler" and gives a melting point of "Approximately 60 °C" (R-MULTI3D-ELECTRIFI-SDS, pp. 1, 3). Inferred filing (the owner's rulings, 2026-10-20, R227, D176): the one biodegradable polyester that melts near 60 °C is polycaprolactone, and its 140-160 °C nozzle and soft, low-modulus filament are a PCL's; the maker names no polymer.
